We call a positive integer a shuffle number if the following hold:

\begin{{enumerate}}
\item All digits are nonzero.
\item The number is divisible by 11.
\item The number is divisible by 12. If you put the digits in any other order, you again have a number that is divisible by 12.
\end{{enumerate}}
Give {k} distinct {n}-digit shuffle numbers.

# Define the digits

# Function to check if a number is a shuffle number
def is_shuffle_number(n):
    # Check if all digits are nonzero
    if '0' in n:
        return False

    # Check if the number is divisible by 11
    if int(n) % 11 != 0:
        return False

    # Check if the number is divisible by 12
    if int(n) % 12 != 0:
        return False

    # Check if the number is invariant under any permutation of its digits
    perms = [''.join(p) for p in itertools.permutations(n)]
    if set(perms) != {n}:
        return False

    return True

# Generate 10-digit shuffle numbers

for i in range(10000000, 999999999):
    n = str(i)
    if is_shuffle_number(n) and len(n) == 10:
        shuffle_numbers.append(n)

# Print the first 50 distinct shuffle numbers
print(', '.join(shuffle_numbers[:50]))
